publishedWalks.title: Highgate Village – “a place apart” — London Walks
stops: Highgate Underground ticket hall: advertised meeting point, not the requested public-exterior anchor
Witanhurst: advertised attraction; complete intermediate itinerary not published
Highgate Cemetery and Kenwood House: explicitly suggested after-walk visits, not confirmed tour stops
themes: Village lanes, cottages, Georgian houses and London views
stories: Advertises associations with Coleridge, Dickens, Betjeman and Dick Whittington, among others, without publishing the individual stories. Origin: commercial tour operator; publication date unknown. Locator: page lines 78–92. Treat as advertised coverage, not historical corroboration. ([walks.com](https://www.walks.com/our-walks/highgate-village-a-place-apart))

publishedWalks.title: The Highgate Village Self-Guided Walk — Richard Jones
stops: Church House and Highgate Literary and Scientific Institute
Holly Lodge Estate and Holly Village
stories: Includes Dickens family lodging, horn-swearing, Coleridge and Gillman, and Whittington tradition. Distinguishes some conjectural literary identifications and pub traditions from firmer claims. Advertised duration: two hours; not a Highgate-station loop. Origin: Richard Jones/commercial publisher; publication date unknown. Locators: lines 51–200. Historical claims require independent verification. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

publishedWalks.title: Lady’s Beautiful Highgate Walk and Map — A Lady in London
stops: Church Road, Talbot Road and Park House Passage
North Hill and passage beside The Wrestlers
Southwood residential streets and Cholmeley Park
Highgate High Street and The Bank
Swain’s Lane and Highgate Cemetery exterior
themes: Woods, parks, viewpoints, shops and pubs
stories: Primarily an observational itinerary rather than detailed historical storytelling. Cemetery admission and swimming are optional excursions, not necessary components. Advertises two to three hours and finishes at Tufnell Park. Origin: travel blog; September 2022 URL, exact publication day not established. Locators: lines 26–91. ([aladyinlondon.com](https://www.aladyinlondon.com/2022/09/highgate-walk.html))

publishedWalks.title: North Hill Challenge — Highgate Society
stops: Highpoint at North Hill/North Road: start
themes: Changing housing provision and building technology
stories: An approximately 800-yard architectural walk covering 34 buildings; chronological numbering differs from walking order. Includes remodelled older fabric, council housing and modernist flats. Origin: local civic society; document date unknown. Locators: PDF pages 1–2, 10–15. Interpretive social explanations and superlatives are not independently verified. ([highgatesociety.com](https://www.highgatesociety.com/media/docs/North%20Hill%20descriptions.pdf))

candidates.name: Highpoint, 1 North Hill
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: modernist housing beyond the village stereotype. The Society identifies Lubetkin and Tecton and contrasting buildings. Anchor proposal: public North Hill pavement, not private entrance or gardens. Locator: PDF page 14, lines 853–896; verify architectural history independently. ([highgatesociety.com](https://www.highgatesociety.com/media/docs/North%20Hill%20descriptions.pdf))

candidates.name: 41 North Hill
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: old fabric versus a later-looking exterior. The Society attributes sixteenth-century origins to a plaque while qualifying subsequent remodelling. Anchor proposal: public pavement opposite the facade. Locator: PDF page 2, lines 75–87; plaque and dates unverified. ([highgatesociety.com](https://www.highgatesociety.com/media/docs/North%20Hill%20descriptions.pdf))

candidates.name: 99 North Hill
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: early municipal housing in an affluent-looking district. The Society attributes this house to Hornsey Council around 1902. Anchor proposal: public pavement, preserving residents’ privacy. Locator: PDF page 11, lines 653–681; legal generalisations need separate checking. ([highgatesociety.com](https://www.highgatesociety.com/media/docs/North%20Hill%20descriptions.pdf))

candidates.name: Montgomery House, Hillcrest Estate
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: post-war municipal rebuilding. The Society attributes the block to Thomas Bennett for Hornsey Council. Anchor proposal: a verified public boundary viewpoint, not assumed estate access. Locator: PDF pages 15–16, lines 931–953; public sightline remains unresolved. ([highgatesociety.com](https://www.highgatesociety.com/media/docs/North%20Hill%20descriptions.pdf))

candidates.name: Rowlands Close, North Hill
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: interpreting interwar flats from their exterior. The Society offers alternative explanations for balconies rather than a settled purpose. Anchor proposal: public North Hill pavement. Locator: PDF page 12, lines 735–759; retain that uncertainty. ([highgatesociety.com](https://www.highgatesociety.com/media/docs/North%20Hill%20descriptions.pdf))

candidates.name: Pond Square
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: an absent landscape feature behind a familiar place-name. Advertised by multiple surveyed walks; historical infilling needs corroboration. Anchor proposal: unobstructed public square edge. Locator: Jones lines 84–87 and London Walks line 92. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Highgate Literary and Scientific Institute, 11 South Grove
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: neighbourhood institutions of shared learning. Jones dates its foundation to 1839. Anchor proposal: public South Grove pavement; interior access unnecessary. Locator: lines 93–97; institutional records needed. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: The Flask exterior
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: separating an displayed date from building history. Jones explicitly qualifies the pub’s dating. Anchor proposal: public pavement, not customer seating. Locator: line 111; avoid promoting alleged patron anecdotes to fact. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: 3 The Grove, Coleridge-associated exterior
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: literary residence and care rather than celebrity enumeration. Jones links Coleridge with the Gillman household. Anchor proposal: public street viewpoint respecting the private home. Locator: lines 122–124; chronology and medical framing require stronger evidence. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Waterlow Park and Lauderdale House exterior
candidates.why: Proposed discovery: philanthropic public landscape, with a present-day hillside view. Friends of Waterlow Park describes Waterlow’s gift and the 1891 opening. Anchor proposal: verified public park path near the house, no interior visit. Locator: lines 37–40; gates close at dusk and exact viewpoint remains unverified. ([waterlowpark.org.uk](https://www.waterlowpark.org.uk/the-park/))

Question affecting selection: should the loop prioritise North Hill housing and architectural change, or the village institutions and Waterlow landscape? These are competing provisional emphases; all ten candidates are alternatives, not compulsory stops.
Question affecting route interpretation: which public exterior station exit should be the precise shared start/end anchor? No exit geometry or safe standing area has been verified.

Route blockers: coordinates, pavement standing areas, crossings, permitted estate-boundary views, park gates, actual route distance, gradients and return directions remain unverified. Landmark names are not standing-point coordinates or camera locations.

Timing remains unknown because no route or audio exists. Preserve the 3,600-second target and requested estimated 55–65-minute range; later accounting must include actual measured narration, walking, crossings, pauses and return to the station. Published-tour durations are not measurements for this job.

Several source dates are unknown; source retrieval occurred for this fresh survey, not as eyewitness observation. Period social explanations must not become distinctive local anecdotes without local supporting evidence.

Usage: 5 hosted-web calls containing 6 search queries, 13 open requests and 1 click request; the click failed. Direct paid spending: USD 0. No paid provider setup was attempted. Elapsed generation time and provider-internal accounting are unavailable rather than estimated.

Infrastructure blockers: docs/ISSUES.md, bundled map access, local renderer and Scout tools were not provided. Their checks cannot be claimed complete. AI provenance, saved map, planned directions, manual playback/navigation fallback and independent final fresh verification remain later-stage requirements.

Recommended next action: retain these stable candidate IDs, resolve the station anchor and thematic selection, then undertake bounded primary-source verification and fresh route geometry for the shortlisted loop. Fix directions and timing before Scout or synthesis; do not begin broad additional research after route acceptance without a named blocker.
